problem: A well pumps a thin poroelastic aquifer. The drawdown spreads radially and the layer contracts, splitting its volume change between areal and vertical strain.
result: RMS errors: 0.71% in pressure, 1.97% in areal strain and 1.90% in vertical strain, relative to the largest analytical values.
scope: 3D quarter slab, 5 m mesh, four times while the front stays inside. RMS errors by mesh (pressure, areal, vertical): 20 m: 2.29%, 3.94%, 5.55%; 10 m: 0.85%, 2.51%, 2.53%; 5 m: 0.71%, 1.97%, 1.90%. (a) pressure drawdown; (b) strain split; (c) mesh convergence.
meaning: This checks two-way coupled pumping deformation against the thickness-averaged model. It does not remove the $O((B/r)^2)$ slab-model difference, which remains at the finest mesh.
